steps.text: Place whole sweet potato in pot and cover with water; bring to a boil. Cook until tender when pierced with a fork, 40 to 50 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Drain the sweet potato and cool briefly under cold running water. Remove and discard the skin. Break sweet potato flesh apart and place in a bowl. Add butter and mix with an electric mixer until well combined.
Add sugar, milk, eggs, nutmeg, cinnamon, and vanilla; beat on medium speed until mixture is smooth.
Pour filling into unbaked pie crust.

Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes. Loosely cover the crust edges with aluminum foil if they begin to brown too quickly. The pie will be puffed like a soufflé when it comes out of the oven but will deflate as it cools. Let pie cool completely before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato Pie
raw_recipe.description: This homemade sweet potato pie is a Southern recipe that makes a smooth and creamy sweet potato filling flavored with cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla in a flaky crust for a classic holiday dessert.

video.description: With autumn just around the corner, this classic baked pie is the perfect dessert to ring in the season. In this video, the Allrecipes team shows you how to make an easy recipe for homemade sweet potato pie. Using fresh cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla to bring an extra sweetness to the rich flavor of sweet potato, it’ll be hard to pass up on a second plate of this delicious dish.

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe for the past three years and always receive rave reviews. People who have eaten sweet potato pie all their lives say this recipe is the best they have ever tasted. I have made minor changes to suit my taste. I use evaporated milk instead of regular milk. I add a 1/4 tsp of cloves and ginger and 2 tbsp of lemon juice. The lemon enhances the tast of the potatoes. I also add a 1 tbsp flour to the mixture to thicken up a bit. Last, I I halve the white sugar and replace with brown sugar. Try this and you won't be disappointed.

I've made this a few times and the recipient always loves it. One suggestion--don't store the boiled sweet potatoes in the fridge when you don't have time to make the pie right then...it separates a bit and makes the pie grainier than it needs to be. It's much smoother when the directions are followed and it's mixed right after boiling and peeling. :)

Best pie I ever made. My Mom flipped, now I have to make it more than once a year. Tip: to get rid of the strings use an electric mixer, the strings stick the beater and not in the pie!! Update: 1. Sun whipping creamnfor the milk itmakse the custard super creamy. 2. Used browned butter and its OVER THE TOP delicious!

This recipe deserves more than 5 stars. Im not a fan of sweet potato pie. For our church holiday bake sale it was a requested. After searching for the best available recipe, I fell in love with this one. I read a lot of the reviews and made some minor adjustments. I used caned sweet potatoes (just as good as the real deal) it was a 29 oz. can (1Ib 13 oz.) As other reviewer suggested, I added 1 tab of shifted flour to the batter and let me tell you, the pie was silky soft and just perfect!

I’ve made this recipe a bunch of times now. It’s become very popular. I did take the liberty to tweak it a little bit. First, I use just over a pound (1.13 to 1.24 lbs) of sweet potato or yam. In fact, I’ve come to find that doing half sweet potato and half yam is the best. I also use the skins in my pies. Just cut them up into small pieces. Second, I have been using a 10 inch graham cracker pie crust. Keebler makes one and it tends to be pretty good. Especially if you’re not making your own. Third, I use a half cup of light brown sugar instead of one cup of white sugar. I also add 1/4 teaspoon of all-purpose white flour and 1/4 teaspoon of baking soda because the brown sugar adds moisture. But my last pie I added a 1/2 teaspoon of King Arthur’s pancake mix instead of flour and baking soda. Fourth, I use my hand mixer with the regular beaters to mix it very well. Then I switch the the whisks and mix it for another 30 seconds da to a minute. Then back to the regular beaters for a little bit more. I do t know why I do this, but it just seems right. 🤷🏼‍♂️

My husband said this sweet potato pie was FABULOUS & just like his mom’s. I reduced the sweetness: 1/2 cup sugar + 1/4 cup brown sugar. Also, I made two pies: one, as others suggested by whipping the eggs separately & folding them into the batter and the second pie, adding eggs as the directions stated. My husband liked the pie the way the directions were written (not whipping eggs separately). I also added pecans to the top & baked 70 minutes, instead of 60 min. IT’S SO YUMMY!

Used this recipe which is great with modifications. No added sugar, they're sweet potatoes -😉. No added salt, salted butter -😉. Crust: 1-1/4 cup oatflour, 6 tblsp salted butter, 6 tblsp ice water. Food processor 10 secs low speed, done. Spread into a butter greased 9" pan Filling: 3 sweet potatoes, 1/2 cup 2% lactose free milk, 1/4 stick of soft salted butter, 2 whole eggs, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1/4 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp real vanilla. Mix in food processor about 30 secs until smooth. Scoup into the crust, bake at 375 for 1 hr. Fluffy and delicious.

First time I’ve ever made or consumed sweet potato pie! I was short on ingredients, so I used remaining white sugar, light and dark brown sugar. Literally every last grain of sugar we had. I only made because our sweet potatoes were going to go bad. I also used almond milk. I didn’t tell my kids what it was and they thought it was the best pumpkin pie they ever had! Then I told them and they didn’t believe me. Since then I’ve made the pie a dozen times! I double the recipe and make 2 pies! I par bake my pie crust first, use 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup light or dark brown sugar, 6 eggs. I don’t weigh or count my yams or sweet potatoes but I make sure I have plenty and leftovers I bake with no crust. Super easy, love it!

I made this recipe. I used twice as much sweet potato so I could make two pies but two pounds of sweet potato was not quite enough. I used half as much sugar (we don't like super sweet things) and I used three eggs but I used all the suggested amounts of everything else for one pie except we didn't have vanilla extract. Having said all of that, this was super easy to make once the potatoes were boiled, cooled and skinned. The filling took twice as long to set. I had to bake the pies for two hours. Final verdict: Delicious. Simply delicious. MUCH better than you can buy in the grocery store and more flavorful than a pumpkin pie. I also made whipped cream from scratch. This is my go-to recipe for Thanksgiving pie from now on. Five stars.
I made this with 2 modifications. I used sweet condensed milk, and I brushed my crust with melted butter and brown sugar before adding the filling .

So I did this recipe on a whim after getting some giant sweet potatoes. I ended up tripling the recipe. first time I've ever made one, and it was the best I've ever had. Instead of a traditional crust, I threw some stale molasses cookies and Trader Joe's Gingersnaps in the food processor with margarine and coated the bottom of my glass dish. Substituted margarine for butter, almond milk for milk, and measured the vanilla extract and spices with my heart. Baked at 300° for 1 hour, 40 minutes, did the toothpick test, and let it cool. It cracked as it cooled, but was otherwise perfect.

Highly suggest making with a gingersnap crust!
Easy and delicious
Awesome recipe, I used a 1/4 teaspoon of ginger with it. The flavors are amazing. Great recipe
We love sweet potatoe pie, and I just made this today! The only thing I changed was I used white sweet potatoes. Love this, definitely a keeper!!

This came out delicious, plenty sweet enough, smooth and creamy. I used ¼ c. white sugar, ¼ c. brown sugar (half the sugar in recipe), ¼ c. soy milk, ¼ c Greek yogurt and 2 tsp vanilla. Baked for 65 minutes, knife not quite clean but crust browning. I mixed in the blender starting with the sweet potato and butter. Used 16. 08 oz of raw sweet potato, which cut a bit and boiled. Next time I would blend in two batches.

This was not a success. The taste was okay, but the texture was way too mushy (see photo), to the point where it was even hard to pick up a slice without it falling apart into gloop. I used canned sweet potatoes to save the 45 minutes of extra cooking time - maybe that was a mistake? I didn't drain them because they didn't seem especially liquidy. I checked it was done by inserting a toothpick into the center. This took multiple tries and extensions of the timer - ended up having to cook it for 1h40m (and it was *still* mushy!)
No change
It’s so good. I used Greek yogurt instead of milk because that’s all I had. It turned out really smooth and delicious.

I made as directed. I'd change the way I made it to have the potatoes cooked in the oven to carnalize them. I personally wanted to add more sugar, maybe like 1/4 of brown sugar as well as the regular 1 cup of sugar. Then make sure to blend it good. I used a KitchenAid and I still think it could have been smoother. But overall not bad. Maybe it will be better cold.
Didn’t work for me. Maybe cause I’m a Brit and the ingredients just don’t transfer. Once I added the milk it just became a drink and wouldn’t solidify enough. I tried.
